items.text: ACME runs spherical diffusion flame tests in drop towers (free-fall tubes) and aboard the International Space Station.
items.excerpt: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests in drop towers and aboard the International Space Station.

items.text: ACME BRE initially observes flames in microgravity without varying the fuel flow rate.
items.excerpt: The flames will initially be observed without varying the fuel flow rate.

items.text: ACME BRE observed quasi-steady burning corresponding to PMMA and Nylon in microgravity despite no airflow.
items.excerpt: Quasi-steady burning corresponding to various condensed-phase materials (such as PMMA and Nylon) was observed in microgravity despite the absence of air flow, where the cessation of ventilation is an established step in putting out spacecraft fires.

items.text: ACME BRE reports that without airflow, 21% oxygen flames self-extinguished in a short time, while elevated-oxygen flames kept burning.
items.excerpt: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.

items.text: At ISS's 21% oxygen, ACME BRE reports microgravity flames without airflow self-extinguished in a short time.
items.excerpt: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.

items.text: ACME CLD Flame plans to study methane and ethylene diffusion flames across a wide range of test conditions.
items.excerpt: Experimentally, we plan to study methane and ethylene diffusion flames over a wide range of test conditions.

items.text: ACME E-FIELD Flames applies up to 10 kV between a burner and a mesh above it to test gas flames in microgravity (near-weightless).
items.excerpt: An electric field is generated by creating a high voltage (up to 10 kV) differential between the burner and a flat circular mesh suspended above (i.e., downstream of) the burner.

items.text: ACME s-Flame issues fuel and diluent mixtures through a spherical porous burner and ignites them to form a nominally spherical flame.
items.excerpt: A series of experiments is proposed in which mixtures of various gaseous fuels and diluents will be issued into an oxidizing environment through a spherical porous burner and ignited to obtain, nominally, a spherical, one-dimensional stabilized flame.

items.text: BASS-II mounted fuel samples in a small wind tunnel with airflow up to 40 cm/s aboard the International Space Station.
items.excerpt: Fuel samples were mounted inside a small wind tunnel which could impose airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s.

items.text: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids) ran its tests aboard ISS inside the Microgravity Glove Box.
items.excerpt: The experiment was conducted aboard the International Space Station (ISS) inside the Microgravity Glove Box (MSG).

items.text: PSI reports BASS aimed to assess an inert gaseous extinguishing agent similar to the one already used on ISS.
items.excerpt: The two main objectives for BASS are to: 1.) Begin to bridge the gap between the normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test#1 method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity. The relation between these can be investigated by observing flames burning for the longer times available in flight. Practical, realistic (thicker) fuels in typical geometries will be examined, including wake flames which have characteristics of a fire burning behind another object (for example, a fire burning in tight area which may not be easily accessible). 2.) Assess the effectiveness of an inert, gaseous extinguishing agent (similar to that used on ISS) in putting out flames over different materials, geometries, preheating, and flow.

items.text: CFI examines combustion of n-dodecane fuel and fuel mixtures at pressures from 0.25 atm to 5 atm.
items.excerpt: The objectives of this investigation are to: 1) Examine the combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane at pressures ranging from 0.25 atm to 5 atm. 2) Analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior. 3) Examine the behavior of combustion characteristics. 4) Investigate the relationship between droplet size, pressure, and flame extinction, and (5) understand the consequence of soot formation during cool flame combustion.

items.text: DAFT-2 modified a TSI P-Trak particle counter for microgravity (near-weightless) and compared it with a DustTrak on orbit.
items.excerpt: The experimental approach consists of the following components: 1) Modification of Instrumentation: TSI P-Trak was modified for use in microgravity by redesigning the condenser tube to use capillary forces for recycling isopropyl alcohol and removing the mercury switch responsible for detecting instrument orientation. 2) Aerosol Generation: Arizona Red Dust (ARD) was chosen as an aerosol standard due to its ease of dispersion. The ARD was aerosolized with GN2 to create particle samples. The aerosol was contained within 15-liter Mylar bags. 3) On-Orbit Testing: The modified P-Trak gathered data from counting aerosol particles and these data were compared to the DustTrak CNC specifically designed to work in microgravity.

items.text: PSI reports the study combined image processing, experimental diagnostics, and detailed soot modeling of SPICE flame data.
items.excerpt: The approach was to combine image processing, experimental diagnostics, and detailed soot modeling.

items.text: PSI reports two-color tomography methods produced 3D reconstructions of soot and temperature fields from BASS and BASS-II imagery.
items.excerpt: Experimental imagery found in PSI from the BASS and BASS-II investigations was post-processed using newly developed two-color tomography methods with DSLR cameras, enabling 3D reconstructions of soot and temperature fields for direct comparison to model predictions.

items.text: FLEX-2 varied chamber pressure from 0.5 to 3.0 atm and oxygen from 0.1 to 0.4 mole fraction.
items.excerpt: The chamber was filled with the appropriate atmosphere, which was varied in pressure between 0.5 atm to 3.0 atm and O2 concentration between 0.1 to 0.4 mole fraction with the diluent gas making up the balance.

items.text: FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) ignites and observes burning of relatively large liquid fuel droplets.
items.excerpt: The FLEX experiments involve igniting and observing the burning behavior of relatively large droplets.

items.text: FLEX reports that at some ambient conditions, extinction droplets were too small to observe or measure with available diagnostics (measuring tools).
items.excerpt: There were ambient conditions where the extinction droplet sizes at all ambient oxygen mole fractions were too small to either be observed or measured with the available diagnostics.

items.text: SAFFIRE-I performed a fire test on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it left the ISS.
items.excerpt: The Saffire-1 experiments was performed on the Orbital Science's Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.

items.text: SAFFIRE-II performed its fire test on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.
items.excerpt: The Saffire-II experiment was performed on the Orbital Science's Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.

items.text: For the ISS (microgravity, near-weightless), PSI hypothesizes that Earth-based fire standards carry significant uncertainty for spacecraft fire safety design.
items.excerpt: This investigation hypothesizes that due to large differences between fire behavior in normal and reduced gravity, the use of terrestrial fires and fire standards to design spacecraft fire safety systems presents an inherent risk to the vehicle because of the significant level of uncertainty.

items.text: SAFFIRE-III burned samples inside the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it undocked (separated) from the ISS.
items.excerpt: The Saffire-III experiments were performed on the Orbital Science's Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.

items.text: For the ISS (microgravity, near-weightless), SAFFIRE-III hypothesizes that Earth fire standards carry uncertainty for spacecraft fire safety design.
items.excerpt: This investigation hypothesizes that due to large differences between fire behavior in normal and reduced gravity, the use of terrestrial fires and fire standards to design spacecraft fire safety systems presents an inherent risk to the vehicle because of the significant level of uncertainty.

items.text: SAME-R sought to quantify the sizes liquid smoke particles reach in low gravity (near-weightless) and relate them to smoke generation conditions.
items.excerpt: Similar to the original SAME investigation, the primary objective of the SAME-R investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and to relate the droplet size distribution to the smoke generation and smoke transport conditions in the experiment.

items.text: PSI hypothesizes that changed smoke particles in microgravity could leave some smoke detectors without an alarm, a fire-detection concern for ISS.
items.excerpt: The change in the size distribution and number density will, in turn, affect the response of the smoke detectors and possibly result in some detectors not producing an alarm when exposed to this smoke.

items.text: SAME turned on an igniter for 15 to 60 seconds and started thermophoretic samplers to collect smoke.
items.excerpt: The operator then ran the self diagnostic procedures on the two smoke detectors and activated the video cameras, turned on the igniter for a predefined period of time (15 to 60 seconds), and initiated the thermophoretic soot samplers to sample the smoke.

items.text: ISS smoke detectors were designed from 1-g (normal Earth gravity) test data since no microgravity data existed, unlike PSI SAME's low-gravity measurements.
items.excerpt: Due to the complete absence of microgravity data, all three of these detector systems were designed based upon 1-g test data and experience.

items.text: SLICE captured more than 4,000 high-resolution images across 13 testing experiments.
items.excerpt: More than 4,000 high-resolution images were captured across 13 testing experiments.

items.text: SPICE ignited flames in controlled co-flow air using burner diameters of 0.41, 0.76, and 1.6 mm.
items.excerpt: Each flame was ignited in a controlled co-flow air environment, with burner diameters of 0.41 mm, 0.76 mm, and 1.6 mm and co-flow velocities ranging from 5.4 cm/s to 65 cm/s.

items.text: Simulates how dibutyl-phthalate (DBP, a liquid) particles form and grow in Earth gravity and microgravity.
items.excerpt: The formation and growth of dibutyl-phthalate (DBP) particles in Earth gravity and microgravity environments was simulated.

items.text: PSI reports a 3-D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model of n-alkane (straight-chain fuel) droplet cool flames in microgravity (near-weightless).
items.excerpt: OpenFOAM was used to develop a 3-D CFD model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density Navier–Stokes flow with low-temperature combustion chemistry, coupled heat and mass transfer, and radiation.

items.text: PSI reports three numerical models of how oxygen concentration affects cool flame (low-temperature flame) extinction limits, using FLEX flight conditions.
items.excerpt: Using the experimental conditions of FLEX flight, a comparative studies of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted using three different numerical modeling schemes, (a) spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture, (b) one dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames using an arc-length continuation method and (c) simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

items.text: PSI-142 modelling shows warm flames have a double reaction zone and play a critical role in cool-to-hot flame transition.
items.excerpt: The results showed that the warm flame has a double reaction zone structure and plays a critical role in the transition between cool flames and hot flames.

items.text: PSI-142 modelling shows flammable regions of warm and cool flames expand as pressure rises, due to higher low-temperature reactivity.
items.excerpt: At elevated pressures, it was found that the flammable region of warm flames and cool flames expands due to the increase in low-temperature and intermediate-temperature reactivity with pressure.

items.text: ACME CFI-G performs spherical diffusion flame (flames fed by gas mixing at the edge) tests aboard the International Space Station.
items.excerpt: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests aboard the International Space Station.

items.text: Without airflow, PSI-20 ACME BRE gas-burner flames at 21% oxygen went out quickly, unlike elevated-oxygen flames; it tested 21 to 40% oxygen.
items.excerpt: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.

items.text: PSI-20 ACME BRE gas-burner flames kept burning without airflow in elevated oxygen in microgravity; Moon's 30% lies inside its tested 21 to 40% range.
items.excerpt: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.

items.text: PSI-20 ACME BRE gas-burner flames kept burning without airflow at elevated oxygen in microgravity; rover's 30% sits in its tested 21 to 40% range.
items.excerpt: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.
